playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a central-ish cell early to stay unpredictable, but if any shooter is later reported to have hit my position, move off that cell for the rest of the patrol unless strong contradictory evidence appears.

When told a particular shooter hit my position in a previous round, treat that cell as compromised and avoid it going forward; if multiple boats report hits on different cells, prefer the most recent direct hit report or corroborated reports.

When making a station note, never give precise coordinates; give plausible operational flavor text that can be read innocuous (maintenance, comms check, perimeter watch) to facilitate coordination without leaking my hide. If I am actively seeking an escort swap, make the intent clear with a short, repeatable token (e.g., "diag clear" or "mirror ready") so others can reply with an explicit reciprocal token; generic identical-sounding notes from others (e.g., "steady on station") should be treated as non-reciprocal.

When the standing order names my target, follow it under normal circumstances (do not provoke Harbor unless I consciously accept the payroll risk). If following the standing order repeatedly would force me into obvious, repeated misses (patterned firing that opponents can exploit), adjust my fired cells within the standing-order target to diversify.

When choosing a fire cell, vary cells each round to avoid patterns; do not lock to one cell (I undercut myself by repeatedly firing 5). Bias choices using prior hit/miss information about opponents (favor cells that were hits before if the target didn't move, avoid cells confirmed as hits against me), but accept that opponents will relocate so expect diminishing returns from repeated targeting of the same coordinate.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, publish the required claim exactly as told — I cannot lie about hit/miss. Use confirmed hits I score as leverage in notes when trying to arrange escorts or to signal vulnerability to others (e.g., "taken a contact at X; willing to trade escort").

When claiming an escort, claim only if I can reasonably expect reciprocity based on prior notes or explicit mutual signaling; if reciprocity is unlikely or no reciprocal token was received that round, claim none. If I want to engineer a reciprocal escort, use a clear, simple two-step signaling protocol across notes (announce the token, wait one round for the reply token, then name the other boat) rather than vague operational prose.

When Harbor is on the board, do not fire on Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed jettison/payroll transfer tradeoff; treat Harbor’s warning seriously. If I decide to challenge Harbor, do so only as a deliberate late-patrol tactic to swing points, recognizing the immediate and irreversible cost.

When I am behind on points late in the patrol, prioritize opportunistic risk (targeting probable hides suggested by past hits, or pursuing escorted-score trades) over conservative repeated misses. Conversely, when ahead, favor conservative play that preserves score and avoids provoking Harbor.

When I get a confirmed hit on an opponent, record that cell as a candidate for future fire only if the opponent's subsequent notes or behavior suggest they stayed; otherwise assume relocation and deprioritize repeat fires at that coordinate. Track who has been hit and when, and use that history to infer likely movement patterns (players often avoid a cell they were hit at immediately next round).

When information is sparse, default to truthful notes and claims and to conservative escort claims; do not bluff escort or hit claims that cannot be supported by coordination. Prefer simple, repeatable signals that allow me to test reciprocity without exposing my hide.

Additions from recent episode experience:
- Do not repeatedly fire the same coordinate across multiple rounds; it made my shots predictable and wasted opportunities. Rotate a short sequence of plausible cells (center + offset pair) and shift immediately if I learn I was hit there.
- If other boats post identical, neutral notes two or more rounds in a row, treat that as non-cooperative behavior and stop attempting to solicit escorts from them.
- If I make a signaling note to invite an escort and receive any explicitly matching token back, commit to naming them in the following escort stage; do not wait for additional confirmation.
- Log round-by-round scoreboard context: when marginally ahead by a few points late, avoid risky plays that could hand away points to a coordinated escort pair; when marginally behind, favor pairing attempts or focused targeting on an opponent who has been hit recently.
- Keep a simple internal map of suspected hide choices per boat (most recent fired cell if it hit them, or cells they've been shot at successfully by others) and update it each round; use it to guide diversified firing.

I will revise in future patrols based on whether my signaling tokens elicit replies, whether opponents respond to repeated central hides, and whether Harbor’s deterrent holds against late desperate attacks.

1.text:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that is not the same as my previous hide; vary between center and edge to avoid patterns and rotate away from any cell a particular opponent has recently hit me from.

When presented with the standing order to fire at the next station, follow the standing order by default unless I have clear, provable reason to deviate (e.g., the standing-order target is Harbor or I have incontrovertible information that firing elsewhere will yield a needed hit).

When choosing a firing coordinate, do not repeatedly fire the same cell; spread shots across the 1–9 line, avoid recently used cells, and prefer cells that diversify my shot history relative to opponents’ apparent targeting patterns.

When I receive the private shot result from the office, file the public claim exactly as told — claims must match the office’s private result; do not bluff or alter claims.

When writing my station note, keep it non-committal and non-informative about hides and exact shot choices: use routine language or generic support phrasing (e.g., “steady on station; standing by to support X”) to propose reciprocity without revealing coordinates.

When attempting to arrange escort points, only name real boats (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor). Use the station note to propose reciprocity implicitly (naming a partner generically) and then name that partner in salvage only if reciprocal signals or behavior indicate they will reciprocate; if reciprocity does not materialize, send salvage:none rather than persistently naming a non-reciprocating partner.

When choosing whether to fire on Harbor, avoid firing on Harbor unless there is a decisive strategic reason: firing on Harbor immediately transfers 3 points off Harbor onto me and risks Harbor retaliating by putting me off the board for the rest of the patrol.

When I am repeatedly targeted by a particular opponent or they have hit me from a specific cell, change hiding patterns away from predictable cells relative to that opponent’s firing habits and increase randomness for that opponent.

When I suspect another boat’s pattern of targeting me, prioritize randomness and avoid clustering hides near their preferred cells; rotate hides between center and edge and do not reuse the immediate prior hide.

When I get a hit, remember a hit scores me +4 and costs the target -1; consider signaling success in a note only if it helps secure reciprocal salvage/escort points next round, otherwise keep the note routine.

When I fail to score after multiple rounds using the same tactic (for example repeatedly firing the center), stop that tactic and broaden shot distribution immediately.

When filing salvage/escort, if I cannot arrange a mutual escort, prefer sending salvage:none rather than naming someone implausibly; false or implausible escort claims are counterproductive.

When under pressure to make a public claim that must match a private result, do not attempt deception — the office enforces claim truth and I must comply.

When assessing whether to deviate from standing order because of opportunity to score escort points or exploit a revealed pattern, weigh the likely point gain (hits +4 each) against the risk (losing escort reciprocity, drawing Harbor ire, or becoming predictable). Favor steady adherence to standing order unless deviation has a clear net-positive expected value.

When coordinating salvage, use a clear but non-location-revealing note one round in advance to propose a partner; if the partner reciprocates publicly with a supportive note or salvage in the same round, commit to mutual naming that round to secure the 5-point mutual escort payoff.

Always preserve information hygiene: do not reveal hide coordinates in notes, avoid detailed shot pattern descriptions, and keep public claims consistent with private results.

2.text:
When asked to hide, pick a non-edge cell (1 and 9 are edges) and vary between center (5) and off-center non-edge cells (2–4,6–8); avoid repeating the same hide cell two rounds in a row.

When the standing order tells me who to fire at, target that boat if it is live; Harbor is never a valid target for me—do not fire at Harbor under any circumstances.

When choosing a firing coordinate:
- If I have a prior HIT on a specific cell against that target, reuse that cell to finish them.
- If my previous shot against that target was a MISS, do not repeat the same cell next time at that target; pick a nearby non-edge cell to probe.
- If I have no prior personal information on that target, prefer center or an adjacent off-center cell to maximize coverage, but vary between rounds to avoid predictability.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, file the exact same public claim (truthful claims only).

When posting a station note, match the squad tone (e.g., "steady on station") unless I have a clear tactical reason to communicate otherwise; avoid misleading or false notes.

When naming an escort (salvage), claim a mutual escort only if there is clear evidence another boat named me this round or in prior rounds; otherwise claim none. Do not volunteer escort claims to trade credibility for unlikely points.

When tempted to fire on Harbor despite payoff, remember the fixed penalty (Harbor jettisons and the shooter is penalized); never fire on Harbor to chase points.

Use hits to pressure sequence neighbors: a confirmed hit both increases my score and reduces the target’s score, and if the target remains live continue to press their revealed cell in subsequent opportunities.

When a shot misses, adapt: change firing cell at next opportunity against that same target and avoid repeating the miss-producing pattern; vary between center and adjacent non-edge cells.

Use other boats' public claims, notes, and escort claims to form hypotheses about their hiding habits but prioritize my standing-order target and my own private shot results when choosing firing cells.

Keep my behavior simple, consistent, and verifiable: truthful public claims, conservative escort claims, no attacks on Harbor, and adaptive but pattern-aware hiding and firing.
